_note: Layer 1 for Time: statutory working-time rules per country, owned by Pebl compliance. Monthly caps for the UK and Germany are derived from their weekly limits for the demo and marked illustrative. Canada is out of scope for Time (provincial rules), so its timesheets go to HR.

UK.description: 48-hour average working week, 11 hours' rest between working days, a 20-minute break after 6 hours. Overtime premium is contractual.
UK.capNote: monthly cap derived from the 48-hour weekly average

DE.description: 8 hours a day, up to 10 if averaged out; 11 hours' rest; 30-minute break after 6 hours, 45 after 9. Extra hours are logged daily.
DE.capNote: monthly cap derived from the 10-hour day
DE.source: Germany: maximum working hours under the ArbZG

US.paidBreakNote: Short breaks (about 5 to 20 minutes) are paid working time under the FLSA. Only a bona fide meal break of 30 minutes or more, fully off duty, can be unpaid.
US.description: Non-exempt employees are paid 1.5x for hours over 40 in a week. No federal cap on hours. Daily-overtime states such as California are excluded from launch.
US.source: US Department of Labor: Overtime pay

JP.description: Overtime needs an Article 36 agreement; generally capped at 45 hours a month and 360 a year, paid at a 25% premium or more.

CA.coverageNote: Canada sits out of Time for now: hours and overtime rules are set province by province.
